coupling_tests: A-only/B-only/AB for copy-compute, memory-compute, front-end-payload, shared-bank, and synchronization dependencies.
cross_layer_prediction_gates: P1/P2 predicts P3 within 10%; schedule model predicts P4 within 5%; deviations trigger model revision rather than post-hoc explanation.

P0.reason: Qualify timing, warmup, device-identity, idle-device, and launch-floor behavior before accepting any latency.

P1.reason: Measure isolated latency/throughput/service mechanisms with exact instruction-family SASS checks.

P2.reason: Measure resource coupling, contention, cache/bank/occupancy sensitivity, and overlap using A/B/AB controls.

P3.reason: Predict and test production-shaped stage and multi-stage behavior using the P1/P2 model.

P4.reason: Validate the selected candidate in production-exact Harrix/service boundaries and separate GPU, CPU dispatch, and end-to-end latency.

target_questions: What are matched production-shaped latency/throughput curves for tensor, SIMT, SFU, conversion, address, and predicate work, including their concurrency limits?
What are production-shaped useful-byte and transferred-byte service curves at the L2 and device-memory boundaries for this working-set and access geometry?
Is the GPU-event timing system stable and what launch/front-end floor is visible under matched grid/block geometry?
How do register allocation, spills, occupancy, system-register access, and warp collectives constrain the production schedule?
What request-service, L1/shared, bank-conflict, and constant-broadcast behavior is produced by the exact tile and layout?
Which copy/compute and producer/consumer dependencies overlap, and which waits or barriers remain on the critical path?
